assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turned induced proximity into a chemical design principle: small molecules rewire the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins once thought undruggable. It changed what chemists and clinicians can do, with degraders in late-stage clinical trials and a mechanistic explanation (cereblon) for thalidomide-class drugs.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target that underlies molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made decisive later contributions, so a three-person prize leaves out real credit. This is my best-supported configuration from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Roughly 25 years from the first PROTAC, with broad independent validation in academia and industry and a growing clinical pipeline. Clinical approval of a PROTAC is not yet established to my knowledge, so timing could still be considered slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether Ciulli or Gray should displace one of the three proposed laureates
Whether the committee wants to wait for a first approved PROTAC
Facts about clinical status are from memory and not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed non-canonical amino acids at chosen sites using orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. It is a clear molecular-design platform that gave precise control over protein chemistry, and it is used for biosensors, photo-crosslinking, antibody-drug conjugates and biomaterials.
assessment.attribution: Schultz's lab created the first orthogonal pair for site-specific incorporation in living cells, and Wang was the lead on the early work. Chin extended it to eukaryotes, quadruplet codons and whole-genome recoding. Mehl and Yokoyama are also credited; I judge Schultz and Chin as the core, with Wang as the third.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation and wide adoption across laboratories. Interpretation is stable and the method is a standard tool.
uncertainties: Division of credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama
Whether recognition of Chin's later recoding work belongs in the same prize
Recollection of early-paper authorship is from memory

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing chemically converts one DNA base to another without a double-strand break, combining deaminase chemistry with programmable targeting. It is a clean molecular-engineering concept that extends the CRISPR toolbox, with first clinical use in patients.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the concept and the development of both cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead postdoctoral authors. A single-laureate prize is defensible; Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine-deaminase demonstration. I keep the proposal to Liu alone.
assessment.maturity: About a decade old with rapid independent adoption and early clinical results. Long-term safety and efficacy data are still accumulating, so some may view it as early. The 2020 CRISPR prize already recognized genome editing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 prize and with prime editing (B016)
Fair treatment of Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo
Maturity of clinical outcomes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single DNA and RNA molecules electrically, with long reads, direct RNA and modification detection, and portable instruments. It is an analytical chemistry innovation with a transformative effect on biology and diagnostics, and it is a direct example of molecular recognition engineering.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Akeson conceived and demonstrated strand translocation as a sequencing idea, Kasianowicz showed single-stranded polynucleotide detection, and Bayley engineered protein pores. Credit is spread across at least five people, and I cannot confidently say which three are decisive. My choice is Bayley for pore engineering, Deamer for the concept, Akeson for the sequencing demonstration.
assessment.maturity: Commercially mature and widely used for 10+ years with independent confirmation. The attribution argument has been the main barrier rather than the science.
uncertainties: Whether Branton or Kasianowicz should be among the three
Whether the nanopore invention is distinct enough from next-generation sequencing (B011)
Commercial details are from memory

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing transformed biology and medicine by reducing the cost of a genome by orders of magnitude. The chemistry of reversible terminator nucleotides and clonal amplification on surfaces is central. Few chemical inventions have had a larger effect on clinical practice.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa approach with reversible terminators; Rothberg led the 454 pyrosequencing platform on a different principle. Ju and Mayer contributed related chemistry or colony methods. A fair prize needs to pick between technology lineages, and that choice is contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with more than 15 years of dominant use. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry rather than medicine or technology
Which of several competing platform lineages deserves recognition
Role of Ju and Mayer

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programming nanoparticle assembly with DNA, and spherical nucleic acids, established DNA as a designable ligand for materials and diagnostics. Colorimetric DNA detection and gene-regulation constructs show real translation. I am attentive to this because it directly parallels peptide-nanoparticle recognition and biosensing.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group, with Storhoff and Mucic, reported DNA-gold nanoparticle assembly and the colorimetric detection scheme. Alivisatos independently reported DNA-nanocrystal organization at about the same time. I propose Mirkin and Alivisatos; Alivisatos is arguably better justified by nanocrystal science than by this specific discovery alone.
assessment.maturity: About 30 years of work with independent confirmation, but the clinical impact of SNA therapeutics is less established than the diagnostic and materials impact.
uncertainties: Whether Alivisatos is better recognized for nanocrystals as a whole than for this candidate
Limited clinical validation of SNA therapeutics
Whether quantum-dot recognition (2023) reduces appetite for further nanochemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, so their real-world impact is enormous. The optimization of pKa, lipid structure and formulation is molecular design that decided whether nucleic-acid medicines worked in people.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Madden, Hope, MacLachlan) developed the ionizable lipid and formulation foundations, and Anderson and Langer's work expanded lipid libraries and combinatorial discovery. The decisive group is crowded and industry-entangled. I propose Cullis for foundational formulation and Anderson for the lipid discovery.
assessment.maturity: Validated at scale by approved siRNA and mRNA products, though the 2023 Medicine prize covered nucleoside modification and may have reduced the case for further recognition of the vaccine field.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize
Which of many contributors are decisive
Patent and company disputes may complicate fair credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates changed how cells are understood to organize biochemistry without membranes, and bring physical chemistry of polymers and multivalent interactions into cell biology. It has broad impact and links to designed peptide and protein assembly, but I am less sure that the central discovery is chemistry rather than cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed liquid-like P granules and nucleoli; Rosen's multivalent-interaction work gave a physical framework. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded grammar. The three proposed names best reflect the early cell-based and in vitro demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: A fast-growing, independently replicated field, but mechanisms, the generality of liquid-liquid phase separation and its physiological relevance remain actively debated, so it may be premature.
uncertainties: Ongoing controversy about the physiological role of phase separation
Fit with the Chemistry prize rather than Medicine
Fair credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag
